mainTopic: The tragedies and mourning rules of אב, the joy of ט״ו באב, and the rules of נשיאת כפים on fast days, including the ban on a drunk כהן
overview: The amud finishes the משנה's list of five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז and gives the five tragedies of תשעה באב. It then sets out mourning rules that grow stricter as תשעה באב comes closer: less joy from ראש חודש אב, no haircuts or laundry in its week, and a limited meal on ערב תשעה באב. The מסכת ends on a joyful note with ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים, when the girls of ירושלים danced in borrowed white clothes and urged the young men to choose a wife for family and fear of Heaven. The גמרא then goes back to an earlier משנה about נשיאת כפים on fast days, מעמדות and יום הכיפורים, and fills in missing words. It brings a three-way מחלוקת between רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about blessing at מנחה and נעילה, based on the worry that a כהן might be drunk. The final ruling follows רבי יוסי, and a late fast-day מנחה is treated like נעילה. Finally, the גמרא learns that a drunk כהן may not bless from the placement of the נזיר section next to ברכת כהנים. It also uses a פסוק to show that the blessing כהן may still eat grape pits.

steps.title: The rest of the five sad events of the seventeenth of Tammuz
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes listing the five calamities of שבעה עשר בתמוז: the לוחות were broken, the תמיד stopped, the city was breached, אפוסטמוס burned the תורה, and an idol was placed in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tablets were broken, the daily offering stopped, the city walls were breached, אפוסטמוס burned the תורה, and an idol was set up in the Sanctuary.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list it started earlier: five terrible things that happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These five events explain why we fast on שבעה עשר בתמוז. The list mixes events from very different times, from משה רבינו breaking the לוחות to the Roman period. What ties them together is the date, not the era.

keyTerms.meaning: The tablets of the Ten Commandments
The daily offering brought in the בית המקדש every morning and afternoon
Was breached (a hole was broken into the city wall)
An idol or image
The Sanctuary, the main building of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This list belongs to שבעה עשר בתמוז, not תשעה באב. The list for תשעה באב starts in the next line.

phrases.english: The tablets were broken,
and the daily offering stopped,
and the city was breached,
and Apostemos burned the Torah,
and he set up an idol in the Sanctuary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of calamities of שבעה עשר בתמוז begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five calamities happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז, which is why it is a fast day.

steps.title: The five sad events of the Ninth of Av
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five calamities of תשעה באב: the decree that the generation of the desert would not enter ארץ ישראל, the destruction of both בתי מקדש, the capture of ביתר, and the plowing of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On תשעה באב it was decreed that our ancestors would not enter the Land, both Temples were destroyed, ביתר was captured, and ירושלים was plowed over.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a matching list of five terrible events that happened on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like שבעה עשר בתמוז, תשעה באב is a day on which tragedy kept repeating. Counting both destructions as separate events gives five: the decree in the desert, the first בית המקדש, the second בית המקדש, ביתר, and the plowing of the city.

keyTerms.meaning: It was decreed
The בית המקדש was destroyed
A major Jewish city that fell to the Romans in the בר כוכבא revolt
Was plowed over like a field

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the basic reason תשעה באב is the most serious fast of the year.

phrases.english: On the Ninth of Av it was decreed upon our ancestors
that they would not enter the Land,
phrases.notes: This is the decree after the spies' report, that the generation in the desert would not enter ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and the Temple was destroyed the first time and the second time,
and Beitar was captured,
and the city was plowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the list for שבעה עשר בתמוז with a list for תשעה באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five calamities happened on תשעה באב.

steps.title: From the start of Av we lessen joy
steps.stepSummary: Once the month of אב begins, we reduce our joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when the month of Av begins, we cut back on rejoicing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from history to practical rules and starts with the first, widest stage of mourning: the start of the month of אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourning does not start suddenly on תשעה באב. It builds up in stages, and this is the first one. Each following rule is stricter and covers a shorter period.

keyTerms.meaning: From when the month of אב begins
We lessen, we cut back
Joy, rejoicing

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the period called the Nine Days.

phrases.english: From when Av begins
we lessen rejoicing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from listing tragedies to the mourning rules that come from them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ראש חודש אב, joy is reduced.

steps.title: No haircuts or laundry in the week of the Ninth of Av
steps.stepSummary: In the week when תשעה באב falls, haircuts and laundering are forbidden, but on Thursday they are allowed for the honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the week תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair or wash clothes, but on Thursday these are allowed in honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second, stricter stage of mourning: the week of תשעה באב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Haircuts and laundry are banned during this week as a sign of mourning. But when תשעה באב falls on Friday, there is no other chance to get ready for שבת. So on Thursday these things are allowed, because the honor of שבת wins out.

keyTerms.meaning: The week in which (a date) falls
To cut hair
To launder clothes
The honor of שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word שבת means the whole week, not just the day of rest.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
phrases.english: The week in which the Ninth of Av falls
it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the time period and makes the mourning stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Haircuts and laundry are forbidden in the week of תשעה באב, except on Thursday for the honor of שבת.

steps.title: The last meal before the Ninth of Av
steps.stepSummary: On ערב תשעה באב one may not eat two cooked dishes, meat, or wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says one should just make a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב תשעה באב, a person may not eat two cooked dishes, and may not eat meat or drink wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he should change his usual way of eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third and strictest stage, the meal right before the fast, and records a disagreement about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives fixed limits: one cooked dish only, with no meat and no wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to take a softer approach: just make some change from your normal meal. The משנה itself does not spell out what kind of change he means.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before תשעה באב
Two cooked dishes
He should change (from his usual meal)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the special last meal before the fast, called the סעודה המפסקת.

phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av
a person may not eat two cooked dishes,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יְשַׁנֶּה.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: He should change.
phrases.notes: He means change from your normal meal. The משנה doesn't spell out how.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the time further, to the last meal before the fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב תשעה באב: no two cooked dishes, no meat, no wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: one must change from his usual meal.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's view on overturning the bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה requires overturning the bed as mourners do, but the חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה requires people to overturn their beds, but the Sages did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more possible mourning practice. רבי יהודה requires it, and the חכמים reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Overturning the bed is a practice of a mourner after a death in the family. רבי יהודה wanted to treat everyone on תשעה באב like a mourner in this way too. The חכמים did not accept this, so the halacha does not require it.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturning the bed, a mourner's practice
The חכמים did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda requires overturning the bed,
but the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further proposed mourning practice that the majority rejects, closing the section on mourning rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires overturning the bed. The חכמים do not.
steps.whatToRemember: The mourning builds in stages: less joy from ראש חודש אב, no haircuts or laundry in the week of תשעה באב, and a limited meal on ערב תשעה באב. The חכמים did not require overturning the bed.

steps.title: The happiest days: ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says there were no happier days for ישראל than ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים. On those days the girls of ירושלים went out in borrowed white clothes, so no one without her own would be embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: ישראל had no days as joyful as ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים. On them the daughters of ירושלים went out in borrowed white clothes, so as not to embarrass a girl who had none of her own.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from sadness to joy. It ends the מסכת with a description of two very happy days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the mourning of אב, the משנה points to ט״ו באב, a day of great joy in the same month. Everyone borrowed white clothes from someone else. That way a poor girl wearing borrowed clothes would look just like everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The fifteenth of אב (ט״ו באב)
White clothes (כלים here means garments)
Borrowed
To embarrass

steps.confusionAlert: כלים here does not mean dishes or vessels. It means clothes.
steps.whyThisMatters: The מסכת deliberately ends on a note of joy and sensitivity to others' feelings, right after the sad laws of תשעה באב.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There were no days as joyful for Israel
as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur,
on which the daughters of Jerusalem would go out
in borrowed white clothes,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: so as not to embarrass one who does not have.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the mourning laws of אב to the joyful day of ט״ו באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים were the happiest days, with borrowed white clothes worn so no one would be embarrassed.

steps.title: The borrowed clothes needed immersion
steps.stepSummary: All the borrowed garments had to be immersed in a מקוה before being worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the garments require immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a detail about the borrowed white clothes: every one of them needed טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the clothes passed from person to person, any of them might have become טמא. So they all had to be immersed. Even the clothes of a wealthy girl were treated this way, so everyone was equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Require
Immersion in a מקוה to make something טהור

phrases.english: All the garments require immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a halachic detail about the borrowed clothes from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the borrowed white garments required טבילה.
steps.whatToRemember: The מסכת ends with joy: on ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים everyone wore borrowed, immersed white clothes, so no girl was singled out or embarrassed.

steps.title: The girls dance and tell the young men what to look for in a wife
steps.stepSummary: On those happy days the girls of ירושלים danced in the vineyards. They told the young men to look at family and fear of Heaven, not beauty, quoting two פסוקים from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The girls of ירושלים went out and danced in the vineyards. They said: Young man, look carefully at whom you are choosing. Do not look at beauty; look at the family. As the פסוק says, 'Grace is false and beauty is empty; a woman who fears ה׳ is the one to be praised.' And it also says, 'Give her credit for the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her at the gates.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים: the girls danced in the vineyards and called out advice to the young men looking for a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 told us the girls wore borrowed white clothes so that no one would be embarrassed. Now we hear what they said: choose a wife for her family and her fear of Heaven, not for her looks. The two פסוקים from משלי back this up, since grace and beauty pass, but a God-fearing woman and her good deeds earn real praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Dancing (in a circle)
Vineyards
Young man
Beauty, good looks
Family, good lineage
Fear of ה׳

phrases.english: And the daughters of Jerusalem would go out
and dance in the vineyards.
And what would they say?
Young man, please lift up your eyes
and see what you are choosing for yourself.
Do not set your eyes on beauty;
set your eyes on the family.
"Grace is false and beauty is empty;
a woman who fears ה׳, she shall be praised,"
and it also says:
"Give her from the fruit of her hands,
and let her deeds praise her at the gates."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the celebrations of ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The girls danced in the vineyards and urged the young men to choose a wife for her family and fear of Heaven rather than for her beauty.

steps.title: The פסוק from שיר השירים: the wedding day and the day of joy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes with a פסוק from שיר השירים. It explains 'his wedding day' as מתן תורה and 'the day of his heart's joy' as the building of the בית המקדש, and ends with a prayer that it be rebuilt soon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the פסוק says: 'Go out and see, daughters of ציון, King שלמה, with the crown his mother crowned him with on his wedding day and on the day of his heart's joy.' 'His wedding day' is the giving of the תורה. 'The day of his heart's joy' is the building of the בית המקדש. May it be rebuilt quickly in our days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings one more פסוק that fits the theme of the 'daughters' going out, then explains it. This ends the משנה and the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'wedding' in the פסוק is read as the bond between ה׳ and the Jewish people at מתן תורה, and the 'joy of his heart' as the building of the בית המקדש. Many explain that this links back to יום הכיפורים, the day the second לוחות were given. The משנה ends the whole מסכת on a hopeful note with a prayer for the rebuilding of the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)
Crown
Wedding
The giving of the תורה
The building of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends the topic of happy days by linking them to מתן תורה and the בית המקדש, and closes with a prayer that it be rebuilt soon.

phrases.english: And so it says:
"Go out and see, daughters of Zion,
King Shlomo,
with the crown his mother crowned him with
on his wedding day
and on the day of his heart's joy."
"On his wedding day": this is the giving of the Torah;
"and on the day of his heart's joy":
this is the building of the Holy Temple,
may it be built quickly in our days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another פסוק about 'daughters' going out and explains it, closing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'His wedding day' means מתן תורה and 'the day of his heart's joy' means the building of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Fast days have no מוסף, so how are there four blessings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that says the כהנים bless four times a day on three occasions, including at מוסף. It asks how that can be, since fast days and מעמדות have no מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that at three times of the year the כהנים raise their hands to bless the people four times a day. But do fast days and מעמדות have a מוסף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting an earlier משנה about נשיאת כפים and challenges its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four blessings in one day, one of them at מוסף, and applies this to fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכיפורים. Only יום הכיפורים has a מוסף, so the list cannot fit fast days and מעמדות as written. The question is phrased as a question, but it really works as a challenge to the משנה's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
Raise their hands (to give ברכת כהנים)
Public fast days
Groups of ordinary Jews who stood with the כהנים of their week and prayed and fasted
The additional prayer said on שבת and holidays

steps.confusionAlert: This גמרא is not on the משנה just finished. It goes back to a משנה from earlier in the פרק about the כהנים blessing the people.

phrases.english: Gemara: At three times in the year
the priests raise their hands, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of that משנה: four times a day, at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה.

phrases.english: Fast days and the gatherings of the watches:
is there a Musaf on them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא, going back to an earlier משנה in the פרק about נשיאת כפים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that on fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכיפורים the כהנים bless four times, including at מוסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fast days and מעמדות have no מוסף, so the four-blessing list cannot apply to them.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words, and the גמרא fills them in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. On all three occasions the כהנים bless at every prayer, and on one of them (יום הכיפורים) that comes to four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: On three occasions the כהנים raise their hands every time the people pray, and on some of them that comes to four times a day: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה. The three occasions are fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the משנה left words out, and it rewrites the משנה with the missing words added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed משנה separates two ideas. On all three occasions the כהנים bless at every prayer said that day. Four blessings happen only on the occasion that has four prayers, which is יום הכיפורים. This removes the problem of a מוסף on fast days.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing words (the משנה left part out)
And this is what it teaches
Closing of the Gates: the last prayer of יום הכיפורים (נעילה)

phrases.english: The Mishnah is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
At three times, the priests
raise their hands
every time they pray,
and on some of them it is four times a day:
phrases.notes: 'Some of them' means יום הכיפורים, the only one of the three with a מוסף.

phrases.english: Shacharis and Musaf,
Mincha and the Closing of the Gates.
And these are the three times:
fast days, the gatherings of the watches, and Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by filling in the missing words of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading missing words into the משנה (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that all three occasions have four blessings, including מוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three occasions have a blessing at every prayer. Only the one with four prayers, יום הכיפורים, has four blessings.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, but the חכמים limit the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the משנה is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים hold that the כהנים bless at שחרית and מוסף but not at מנחה and נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This is the view of רבי מאיר. But the חכמים say: שחרית and מוסף have נשיאת כפים, while מנחה and נעילה do not.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא tells us whose view the משנה follows and adds the other side, the חכמים, who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר the כהנים bless at every prayer on these days, even late in the day. The חכמים limit it to the morning prayers, שחרית and מוסף, and leave out the afternoon prayers, מנחה and נעילה. So the משנה we just explained turns out to be only one opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the opinion of רבי מאיר
Raising of the hands: ברכת כהנים
The afternoon prayer

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabbah bar Avuh:
This is the view of Rabbi Meir.
But the Sages say:
Shacharis and Musaf
have the raising of the hands;
Mincha and Neilah
do not have the raising of the hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the corrected משנה of step 12 as רבי מאיר's view and gives the חכמים's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי מאיר. The חכמים hold that נשיאת כפים is done at שחרית and מוסף only, not at מנחה or נעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question of the sugya: which view is the halacha for ברכת כהנים at מנחה and נעילה.

steps.title: Who are the Sages who argue with רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'חכמים' are that hold the כהנים bless only at שחרית and מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these Sages?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which specific תנא is behind the 'חכמים' view mentioned in the last step. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רב נחמן said the משנה follows רבי מאיר, and that 'the חכמים' allow ברכת כהנים only at שחרית and מוסף. The גמרא now wants to know exactly who these חכמים are.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
The Sages; here, the unnamed group arguing with רבי מאיר

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the 'חכמים' just mentioned by רב נחמן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which named תנא holds the view of the חכמים (blessing only at שחרית and מוסף).

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא shows three views
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are רבי יהודה. A ברייתא lists three opinions: רבי מאיר says all four prayers get the blessing, רבי יהודה says only שחרית and מוסף, and רבי יוסי says נעילה yes and מנחה no.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה and נעילה all have ברכת כהנים, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: שחרית and מוסף have it; מנחה and נעילה do not. רבי יוסי says: נעילה has it; מנחה does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים are רבי יהודה. It proves this from a ברייתא that lays out three different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא matches the חכמים exactly: yes at שחרית and מוסף, no at מנחה and נעילה. The ברייתא also brings in a third view, רבי יוסי, who splits the afternoon prayers: נעילה gets the blessing, but מנחה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Raising of the hands; the כהנים' blessing of the people
The closing prayer, said at the end of the day on יום הכיפורים and fast days

steps.whatToRemember: Three views: רבי מאיר says all four prayers; רבי יהודה says only the morning ones (שחרית and מוסף); רבי יוסי says everything except מנחה.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught:
The morning prayer, the additional prayer, the afternoon prayer, and נעילה
all of them have the raising of the hands,
this is the view of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: the morning prayer and the additional prayer
have the raising of the hands,

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחָה וּנְעִילָה — אֵין בָּהֶן נְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם.
phrases.english: the afternoon prayer and נעילה do not have the raising of the hands.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נְעִילָה — יֵשׁ בָּהּ נְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: נעילה has the raising of the hands,
the afternoon prayer does not have the raising of the hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and backs the answer with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי יהודה, as the ברייתא shows his view matches theirs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the three תנאים are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the three views. This sets up the explanations of each תנא that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only gave the rulings. Now the גמרא wants the logic underneath, so we can see why each תנא rules the way he does.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the underlying reason)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what the three views are to why they hold them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the three-way מחלוקת in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: no drunkenness today, so bless even at מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that the כהנים usually skip the blessing at מנחה only because they might be drunk. On a fast day no one is drunk, so they bless at every prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: why don't the כהנים raise their hands at מנחה on a normal day? Because of drunkenness. Today (a fast day) there is no drunkenness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's reasoning. The only reason for no blessing at מנחה is fear of drunkenness, and that fear does not exist on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that on a normal day there is no ברכת כהנים at מנחה, because people may have had wine at their meal and a drunk כהן may not bless. רבי מאיר says the rule follows the reason. Since nobody eats or drinks on a fast day, the reason is gone, so the blessing comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Drunkenness
Spread their hands; give ברכת כהנים
Now; here, on the fast day

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
On every ordinary day, what is the reason
that the כהנים do not spread their hands at the afternoon prayer?
Because of drunkenness,
but now there is no drunkenness.
phrases.notes: "Now" means on the fast day, when no one is eating or drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 16 with the first of the three reasons.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי מאיר, the ban at מנחה depends on actual drunkenness, which does not exist on a fast day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a fast day the כהנים bless at all prayers, including מנחה and נעילה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the ban follows the time of day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the Sages made a fixed rule by time of day. Morning prayers, when drunkenness is rare, were never banned. Afternoon prayers, when drunkenness is common, were banned, even on a fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: at שחרית and מוסף, when drunkenness is not common on a normal day, the Sages made no decree. At מנחה and נעילה, when drunkenness is common on a normal day, the Sages made a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's reasoning. The Sages' decree covers every afternoon prayer, whether or not anyone is actually drunk that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה sees the decree as a fixed rule that does not switch off when its reason is missing. Because the afternoon is a time when people are often drunk on ordinary days, every prayer said at that time lost ברכת כהנים. That includes מנחה and נעילה on a fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: Common; happens often
The Sages made a decree (a protective rule)

steps.confusionAlert: There is no נעילה on a normal day. When רבי יהודה says 'מנחה and נעילה of every day,' he means prayers said in the afternoon, the time of day when people are often drunk.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
The morning prayer and the additional prayer, when on every ordinary day
drunkenness is not common,
the Sages did not make a decree about them,
the afternoon prayer and נעילה, when on every ordinary day
drunkenness is common,
the Sages made a decree about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second reason, which disagrees with רבי מאיר by treating the decree as fixed by time of day.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יהודה, the decree covers all afternoon prayers, even on a fast day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ברכת כהנים at מנחה or נעילה, even on a fast day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: מנחה is banned, but נעילה is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that the decree covers מנחה, which is said every day. נעילה is not said every day, so the Sages did not include it in the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: מנחה, which exists every day, the Sages made a decree about. נעילה, which does not exist every day, the Sages did not make a decree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's middle view. The decree is tied to the everyday prayer מנחה, not to the rare prayer נעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי keeps the decree on מנחה even on a fast day, because the fast-day מנחה is the same prayer people say every day. But נעילה is special and is not part of the everyday routine, so the decree was never extended to it, and the כהנים bless at נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It exists; it is said
It does not exist; it is not said

steps.whatToRemember: The three views come down to two questions: does the decree still apply when no one is drunk (רבי מאיר says no), and does it reach a prayer that is not said every day (רבי יוסי says no, רבי יהודה says yes)?
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows three ways to understand a rabbinic decree: it may depend on its reason (רבי מאיר), it may be fixed by time of day (רבי יהודה), or it may be tied to the regular everyday prayer (רבי יוסי).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
the afternoon prayer, which is said every day,
the Sages made a decree about it,
נעילה, which is not said every day,
the Sages did not make a decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third reason, a middle position between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יוסי, the decree applies only to the everyday prayer מנחה, not to נעילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a fast day the כהנים bless at נעילה but not at מנחה.

steps.title: Three Amoraim lean toward רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב, רבי יוחנן and רבא all side with רבי מאיר, but each uses a different term: הלכה, נהגו העם, or מנהג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר. רבי יוחנן said: the people practice like רבי מאיר. רבא said: the custom is like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to how we actually rule in the three-way argument. Three אמוראים all lean toward רבי מאיר, who holds that the כהנים bless at all four prayers on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three agree on whose side to take, but they use three different labels. The labels are not the same thing, and the next step explains how strong each one is.

keyTerms.meaning: The binding law
The people are used to doing it this way
An accepted custom

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Meir.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people practice like Rabbi Meir.
And Rava said:
The custom is like Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the reasons of the three תנאים, the גמרא moves on to the practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three אמוראים side with רבי מאיר, at three different levels of strength.

steps.title: What each level of ruling means
steps.stepSummary: הלכה is taught publicly. מנהג is not taught publicly but is told to someone who asks. נהגו is not even told to someone who asks, but if a person already did it, it counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever said 'הלכה like רבי מאיר' means we teach it in the public lecture. Whoever said 'מנהג' means we don't teach it publicly, but we tell someone who asks. Whoever said 'נהגו' means we don't even tell someone who asks, but if he did it, it counts and we don't make him go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the three labels from the last step differ from each other in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are three levels, from strongest to weakest. הלכה is announced to everyone. מנהג is given only as a private answer. נהגו is not taught at all, but it is accepted after the fact, so the person does not have to repeat the prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach it publicly
The public lecture, usually on שבת
We give it as a ruling to someone who asks
We make him go back and redo it

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of ruling: הלכה (taught to the public), מנהג (told when asked), נהגו (not told, but accepted after the fact).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מנהג and נהגו. Here מנהג is the stronger one: you may tell someone to act that way. With נהגו you only accept it once it has already been done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-level scale is a useful tool for understanding how strong any ruling is.

phrases.english: The one who said "the halacha follows Rabbi Meir"
means we teach it in the public lecture.
The one who said "custom"
means we do not teach it publicly,
but we do rule that way when asked.
And the one who said "the people practice"
means we do not even rule that way,
but if someone did it, it counts,
and we do not make him go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר — דָּרְשִׁינַן לַהּ בְּפִירְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three labels used in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלכה is taught publicly, מנהג is told when asked, and נהגו is only accepted after the fact.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees and says the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: bless at נעילה but not at מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth אמורא gives a different ruling, siding with רבי יוסי instead of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יוסי means the כהנים bless at שחרית, מוסף and נעילה on a fast day, but not at מנחה. The decree against blessing at מנחה stays in force, even on a fast day.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different ruling from the three אמוראים in step 20.

steps.title: The final ruling follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא itself decides: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question and accepts רב נחמן's ruling as the final law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא speaks in its own voice and decides between the opinions. So at the level of law, there is no ברכת כהנים at מנחה, even on a fast day, while נעילה does get the blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: And the law is (the גמרא's final decision)

steps.whatToRemember: The final law follows רבי יוסי: no ברכת כהנים at מנחה, but yes at נעילה.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב נחמן's ruling as the final law.

steps.title: Why do כהנים bless at מנחה of a fast day today?
steps.stepSummary: If we follow רבי יוסי, מנחה should have no ברכת כהנים. So why do כהנים today bless at מנחה on a fast day?
steps.simpleTranslation: Nowadays, why do the כהנים raise their hands to bless at מנחה of a fast day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just accepted by pointing to what people actually do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says there is no blessing at מנחה. Yet the practice is for כהנים to bless at מנחה on a fast day. That seems to go against the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays
Spread their hands, meaning they give ברכת כהנים
The מנחה prayer of a fast day

phrases.english: And nowadays, what is the reason
that the kohanim spread their hands
at the afternoon prayer of a fast day?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא מַאי טַעְמָא פָּרְשִׂי כָּהֲנֵי יְדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 23 based on current practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי (no blessing at מנחה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Current practice is for כהנים to bless at מנחה of a fast day, which seems to go against רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Late מנחה is treated like נעילה
steps.stepSummary: The fast-day מנחה is said close to sunset, so it counts like נעילה, which רבי יוסי allows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they bless close to sunset, it is like the נעילה prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and shows that the practice does fit רבי יוסי after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a fast day, מנחה is pushed late, right before sunset. At that time it looks like נעילה, which is not said every day, so the decree never covered it. That is why the blessing is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset
It is like, it is treated as

phrases.english: Since it is close to sunset
that they spread their hands,
it is like the Ne'ilah prayer.
phrases.notes: This connects to step 19: רבי יוסי allows the blessing at נעילה because it isn't said every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּבְסָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה קָא פָּרְשִׂי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the late מנחה is treated like נעילה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The practice of blessing at the fast-day מנחה goes against רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it is so close to sunset, the fast-day מנחה is like נעילה, so even רבי יוסי allows the blessing.

steps.title: Everyone agrees a drunk כהן may not bless
steps.stepSummary: From all the opinions above, one point is clear to everyone: a drunk כהן may not give ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that a drunk כהן is forbidden to give ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out a point that all three תנאים share. This also sets up the next question, which asks for the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three opinions were built on the worry that a כהן might be drunk. So all of them must agree that a drunk כהן may not bless. They only argue about when that worry applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
In any case, at least
A drunk person
Raising the hands, meaning ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
a drunk person is forbidden to raise his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת שִׁכּוֹר אָסוּר בִּנְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the shared idea behind all three opinions and starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A drunk כהן may not give ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Where is this rule learned from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a drunk כהן may not bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees on the rule, but the גמרא wants to know where it comes from in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a drunk כהן may not give ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Learned from the נזיר section placed next to it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא, says the פרשה of ברכת כהנים is placed right after the פרשה of נזיר to teach that the blessing כהן, like a נזיר, may not drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of בר קפרא: why is the section of the blessing כהן placed next to the section of the נזיר? To teach: just as a נזיר may not drink wine, so a blessing כהן may not drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a source from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר chapter 6, the laws of נזיר come right before ברכת כהנים. Putting them next to each other teaches that they share a rule. Just as a נזיר may not drink wine, a כהן who is about to bless may not drink wine either.

keyTerms.meaning: Was placed next to
The section about the נזיר
A כהן who gives the blessing

steps.whatToRemember: A drunk כהן may not bless. We learn this because the פרשה of ברכת כהנים sits right next to the פרשה of נזיר in במדבר chapter 6.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Bar Kappara:
Why was the section of the blessing kohen placed
next to the section of the nazir?
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:1–21 is about the נזיר, and right after it, 6:22–27, comes ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: To say: just as a nazir is forbidden to drink wine,
so too a blessing kohen is forbidden to drink wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת כֹּהֵן מְבָרֵךְ לְפָרָשַׁת נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two sections are placed next to each other in the תורה, which shows that the blessing כהן, like the נזיר, may not drink wine.

steps.title: If the blessing כהן is like a נזיר, he should also be forbidden grape pits
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דרבי זירא (or אושעיא בר זבדא) attacks the comparison to נזיר. A נזיר may not eat grape pits, so by this logic a blessing כהן should not be allowed to eat them either, which makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא's father, and some say it was אושעיא בר זבדא, challenged this: If the blessing כהן is just like a נזיר, then since a נזיר is forbidden to eat grape pits, a כהן who blesses should also be forbidden to eat grape pits!
steps.whatsHappening: A חכם challenges בר קפרא's comparison between the blessing כהן and the נזיר. He shows that taking the comparison all the way leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is forbidden to have anything from the grapevine, not only wine. If the blessing כהן is learned from the נזיר, he should also be forbidden even something as minor as grape pits. Nobody holds that, so the comparison seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly challenges it. This is a forceful objection to what was just said.
A person who took a vow to avoid all grape products, haircuts, and contact with the dead.
Grape pits, one of the grapevine products forbidden to a נזיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira's father strongly objected to it,
and some say it was Oshaya bar Zavda:
If so, just as a nazir is forbidden in grape pits,
so too a blessing kohen should be forbidden in grape pits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in Step 28, the comparison of the blessing כהן to a נזיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's comparison of the blessing כהן to a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, every נזיר ban, including grape pits, would apply to the blessing כהן. That result is unacceptable.

steps.title: A פסוק compares the blessing כהן to the serving כהן, who may eat grape pits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings the פסוק "לשרתו ולברך בשמו", which links blessing to serving in the מקדש. The serving כהן may eat grape pits, so the blessing כהן may eat them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The פסוק says, "To serve Him and to bless in His name." Just as a כהן who serves is allowed to eat grape pits, so too a כהן who blesses is allowed to eat grape pits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the challenge with a פסוק. It ties the blessing כהן to the כהן serving in the מקדש, not to the נזיר, when it comes to grape pits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "serving" and "blessing" side by side, so the rules of the serving כהן set the limits for the blessing כהן. The serving כהן is permitted grape pits, so the blessing כהן is permitted too. The ban on a drunk כהן blessing stays in place, but it does not stretch to grape pits.

keyTerms.meaning: To serve Him, meaning the עבודה of a כהן in the מקדש.
The one who serves, the כהן doing עבודה.
Permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: A drunk כהן may not give ברכת כהנים. Still, the blessing כהן is compared to the serving כהן, so he may eat grape pits. Only the נזיר is forbidden those.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact limit of the ban: wine disqualifies a כהן from ברכת כהנים, but minor grape products do not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: The verse says:
"To serve Him and to bless in His name,"
just as one who serves is permitted in grape pits,
phrases.notes: "One who serves" is the כהן doing the עבודה in the מקדש.

phrases.english: so too a blessing kohen is permitted in grape pits.

steps.terutzResolutionType: New scriptural source that limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the blessing כהן is like a נזיר, he would be forbidden even grape pits.
